title: Tidying irregulars: the '-go' verbs and their mood tense (-ga); venga, dígame, traer

cards.title: The full panorama
cards.body: Every tense and mood is now covered. Half the course was content, half was how to manage it and find what you've forgotten. Keep listening actively; even recognising verb endings in songs and films helps.

cards.title: The '-go' verbs
cards.body: Older languages collect irregularities, but they come in groups. These verbs use -go only for I in the present: tener (tengo, but tiene, tenemos), venir (vengo), salir (salgo), poner (pongo), decir (digo), hacer (hago), oír (oigo, I hear), traer (traigo, I bring).

examples.en: I have / come / go out / put / say / do / hear / bring
examples.es: tengo / vengo / salgo / pongo / digo / hago / oigo / traigo

cards.title: Mood tense: -go → -ga for everyone
cards.body: Instead of swapping vowels, these verbs build the mood tense on -ga, for every person.

cards.title: ¡Venga! · ¡Dígame!
cards.body: In Spain, venga means 'come on' (and 'venga, vale' ends phone calls). Dígame ('tell me') is how people in Spain answer the phone.

cards.title: traes vs traigas
cards.body: Plain present: traes. Mood tense: traigas.

examples.en: I want you to bring it.
I don't want you to distract me.

practice.en: I want you (informal) to bring it.
